name: Section Headings
explanation: Content should be organized using section headings wherever it's logically divided into distinct parts. This applies to the structure of written content itself, such as an article broken into topics. It doesn't mean labeling every interface widget or control. A long piece of content with no headings at all forces a reader to process it as one undifferentiated block. Headings let someone see its structure and jump to the part they need.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users navigate long content most efficiently by jumping between headings. A lengthy article or document with no heading structure at all forces them to listen through everything in order, with no way to skip to a relevant section. People with cognitive disabilities benefit from headings too. Headings break content into digestible, clearly labeled chunks, since a wall of unstructured text is harder to scan, parse, and return to later.

codeExample.bad:
Complete Guide to Home Gardening

Soil preparation is the foundation of any garden...

Once your soil is ready, choosing the right plants...

Watering schedules vary significantly by plant type...
codeExample.good:
Complete Guide to Home Gardening

Preparing Your Soil

Soil preparation is the foundation of any garden...

Choosing the Right Plants

Once your soil is ready, choosing the right plants...

Watering Schedules

Watering schedules vary significantly by plant type...

howToTest: Read through any long piece of content on the site: an article, a help page, a set of instructions. Check whether it's broken into logical sections with actual heading elements. Bold text or visual spacing that only looks like a heading doesn't count. If a lengthy piece of content has no internal headings at all despite covering multiple distinct topics, this fails.

check.question: A 2,000-word help article covers three distinct topics: account setup, billing, and troubleshooting, but the entire article has only one <h1> at the top and no other heading elements dividing the three topics. Does this pass SC 2.4.10 Section Headings?
choices: Yes, because the article does have one heading at the top
No, because the distinct sections within the content aren't organized with their own section headings
Yes, because paragraph breaks are sufficient to show the structure
It depends only on the total word count of the article
